purpose.title: 1. Purpose of the service
purpose.text: NeuroZen offers tools to manage work stress and connects workers with licensed psychologists. It does not replace emergency care: in a crisis, call the local emergency line or go to the nearest emergency service.

data.title: 2. Data we process
data.text: We process your account data (name, email) and the information you record on the platform, in accordance with Peru's Personal Data Protection Law No. 29733 and its regulations.

health.title: 3. Sensitive health data
health.text: Your stress records and mental health information are sensitive data. They are used only to provide the service, are never sold, and are only seen by a professional when you book a session with them.

professionals.title: 4. Verified professionals
professionals.text: Psychologists can only see clients on NeuroZen after our team verifies their license number and status with the Peruvian College of Psychologists.

rights.title: 5. Your rights
rights.text: You can access, rectify, cancel or object to the processing of your data by writing to info{'@'}neurozen.com.

zenbot.subtitle: Your wellbeing assistant
zenbot.disclaimer: ZenBot gives automated guidance: it doesn't diagnose or replace a professional, and it can't contact emergency services for you.

crisis.title: If you are in danger, get help now:
crisis.region: These lines are in Peru. If you are in another country, call your local emergency number.
crisis.limits: ZenBot can't call or notify anyone for you. If you can, reach out to someone you trust right now and don't stay alone.

answers.welcome:
Hi! I'm ZenBot, your NeuroZen wellbeing assistant. I'm here to help you understand how you feel, manage stress and find resources that can help you.
Choose an option or write to me in your own words.
answers.empty: Write whatever you'd like to tell me and I'll help.
answers.crisis: Thank you for telling me; what you're feeling is very serious and you deserve help right now. Your life matters. If you are in immediate danger or thinking about hurting yourself, call one of these lines or emergency services now, and reach out to someone you trust who can be with you.
answers.fallback: I'm not sure I understood. Could you tell me in other words? You can also tap the options button to see topics I can help with.
answers.fallbackSpecialist: It seems your situation deserves more personal attention than I can give. If you'd like, you can talk to one of our psychologists; meanwhile, I'm still here.
answers.crisisOngoing: I'm still here with you. The most important thing right now is your safety: please contact one of these lines or someone you trust. When you are safe, tell me and we'll continue.
answers.afterCrisis: I'm glad to read that you're safe. If you'd like, you can talk to a NeuroZen psychologist for support over the next few days. I'm here if you need anything else.
answers.riskCheck: What you're writing sounds really hard and I want to understand you well. Are you thinking about hurting yourself or ending your life? You can answer honestly; I won't judge you.
answers.supportAfterCheck: Thanks for clarifying. Even so, feeling this overwhelmed deserves attention: talking to a professional can help ease that weight. I can also guide you through a breathing exercise right now.
answers.supportSuggestion: From what you tell me, this has been affecting you persistently. I can't make a diagnosis, but talking to a psychologist can help a lot; you can see the directory or book an appointment.
answers.more: Sure, here are other options from the library related to what we talked about.

starters.work: I have problems related to my job

resources.loading: Looking for NeuroZen resources for you…
resources.intro: These NeuroZen resources may help you:
resources.none: I couldn't find a specific resource for this in the library. You can explore the full library or try a breathing exercise.
resources.error: I couldn't load the resource library right now. Check your connection and try again; your conversation is kept.

stress.0: I understand. Feeling a lot of stress is exhausting, and it's good that you want to do something about it. We can start by easing the tension of the moment and then look at what's causing it.
stress.1: Thanks for telling me. When stress builds up, it's hard to think clearly; going step by step helps. Here are some tools to get started.

work.0: I understand. When work worries continue even after the workday ends, it can be hard to rest. We can start by identifying which situations put the most pressure on you and try some techniques to help you disconnect.
work.1: Work is one of the most common sources of stress, and you don't have to solve everything at once. Calmly looking at which situations weigh the most is a good first step.

anxiety.0: Feeling anxious or worried can be very uncomfortable. Slow breathing helps your body calm down, and writing down what triggered the worry lets you see it with more perspective.
anxiety.1: It's understandable to feel nervous when a lot is at stake. Let's first try something that gives you a bit of calm right now.

sleep.0: Sleeping badly increases stress and makes everything feel heavier. Disconnecting from screens a while before bed and slow breathing, like 4-7-8, can help you relax.
sleep.1: Rest is key to your wellbeing. Keeping regular hours and a calm routine before bed usually helps; here are some NeuroZen options.

burnout.0: Feeling emotionally exhausted is a sign that you've been giving more than you recover for a long time. You deserve real breaks, not just pushing through.
burnout.1: That tiredness that doesn't go away with sleep can be very frustrating. Short breaks during the day and checking your stress level can be a good start.

relax.0: Great idea! Relaxing is a skill you can train. Guided breathing is an easy way to start: we have mindful, box and 4-7-8 breathing exercises.
relax.1: Relaxing for a few minutes a day makes a difference. Here are NeuroZen exercises and videos to practice.

focus.0: When you're stressed, focusing is harder. Alternating work blocks with short breaks and a few deep breaths helps you regain attention.

assessment.0: The PSS-10 test has 10 questions about the last month and gives you guidance on your perceived stress level (0 to 40). It's not a diagnosis, but it helps you understand yourself better. Your latest result and records appear on your dashboard.

stats.0: On your dashboard you'll see statistics based on your own records and your latest test. If you don't have records yet, you can start by logging how you feel.

triggers.0: Logging what stresses you (when it happened, what occurred and how intense it was) helps you discover patterns and decide what to change.

breaks.0: Active breaks are short pauses to move and stretch during the workday. You can set how often to take them.

resources.0: Sure! I looked in the NeuroZen library for wellbeing exercises and videos that may help you.

talk.0: I'm here to listen. You can tell me whatever you want, at your own pace.
talk.1: Thank you for wanting to share it. Putting words to what you feel is already an important step.

sad.0: I'm sorry you feel this way; your emotions are valid and you don't have to carry them alone.

professional.0: Seeking professional support is a great decision. All NeuroZen psychologists have verified licenses. You can see their profiles or book an appointment in a few steps; nothing is booked without your confirmation.

booking.0: You can book an appointment by choosing a professional, date, time and appointment type. You'll only see the days the professional works, and nothing is confirmed without your approval.

appointments.0: In “My appointments” you can see your appointments, cancel them, share a report with your psychologist and rate completed appointments. Any cancellation will ask for confirmation.

subscription.0: We have Basic, Advanced and Professional plans. You can see what each includes in the subscriptions section.

thanks.0: You're welcome! I'll be here when you need me. 🌿

bye.0: See you soon! Remember to take a moment for yourself today.

help.0: I can guide you about stress, anxiety, sleep, exhaustion or workload, recommend resources from the library and take you to NeuroZen tools: PSS-10 test, trigger log, breathing, active breaks or a psychologist.

greeting.0: Hi! How are you feeling today? You can tell me what's on your mind or choose one of the options.

continue.stress: Thanks for explaining. It makes sense that this stresses you. Something that usually helps is separating what depends on you from what doesn't, and taking short breaks to breathe. Logging these situations will let you see patterns.
continue.work: Thanks for telling me. When work responsibilities pile up, it's normal to feel there isn't enough time. It may help to prioritize what's urgent, set limits on your hours and log the situations that put the most pressure on you so you can discuss or adjust them.
continue.anxiety: I understand. Putting your worry into words already helps give it shape. When the worry comes up, try slow breathing and ask yourself which part is under your control.
continue.sleep: Thanks for the detail. A calm routine before bed, avoiding screens and caffeine at night, and slow breathing when you lie down can help. If it continues over time, it's worth talking to a professional.
continue.burnout: Thanks for telling me. When exhaustion lasts, it's better not to wait for it to pass on its own: real breaks, reviewing your workload and, if you need it, professional support can help you recover energy.
continue.talk: I hear you. Thank you for trusting me with this. What you feel matters. If you'd like, I can suggest something that helps right now or a space to talk it through with a professional.
continue.sad: Thank you for trusting me with this. If that sadness persists or weighs on you a lot, talking to a psychologist can help. Meanwhile, I'm here.
continue.relax: Perfect. Practicing a few minutes every day is what helps most; start with the exercise that feels most comfortable.
continue.focus: I understand. Split the task into small parts and take a short break between each one; that makes it easier to regain focus.
continue.assessment: When you complete the test, your result will appear on your dashboard with its scale (0-40).
continue.stats: Your statistics update with every record you log.
continue.triggers: The more records you have, the better you'll see which situations repeat.
continue.breaks: Scheduling short breaks regularly helps take care of your body and mind during the workday.
continue.resources: If you'd like, I can look for other resources: type “another”.
continue.professional: Whenever you want, you can book from here; nothing is confirmed without your approval.
continue.booking: When you choose an available date, you'll see the professional's free times.
continue.appointments: From “My appointments” you can check the status of each appointment.
continue.subscription: If you have questions about a plan, check its details in the subscriptions section.
